desc: This is a reversed Lomography Redscale film. Redscale stocks are wound backwards, so light enters through the base and hits the red-sensitive layer first, causing the strong red tint. To bypass this, I re-spooled the film the right way, exposing it like regular color negative film. Since these rolls were expired and gifted, it was the perfect chance to experiment and recover more natural colors from an otherwise niche film type. Grain and color shifts may still occur due to age, but that’s part of the charm.
